learn.title: Data that branches
learn.body: A list has one path. A tree branches. It starts at one node called the root. Each node may have children below it, and a node with no children is a leaf. Files in folders, and a family tree, are trees.

learn.title: Binary trees
learn.body: In a binary tree every node has at most two children, called left and right. A node is the parent of its children. The root has no parent. The number of levels from root to the deepest leaf describes how tall the tree is.

learn.title: A tree node
learn.body: It looks like a list node, but with two pointers. A missing child is NULL.

learn.title: A tiny tree
learn.body: `new_node` mallocs a node and sets both children to NULL. Node 5 is the root, and 3 and 8 are its children, which are leaves.

learn.title: Naming the parts
learn.body: The tree has root 5, children 3 and 8 of the root, and 1 and 4 as children of 3.
steps: 5 is the root, with no parent
3 and 8 are children of 5, so 5 is their parent
1, 4 and 8 have no children, so they are leaves

questions.prompt: What is the first node of a tree called?
questions.explanation: The root is the top node, the only one without a parent.

questions.prompt: What is a node with no children?
questions.explanation: Leaves are at the ends of the branches.

questions.prompt: A binary tree node has at most \_\_ children.
questions.explanation: Binary means two: a left and a right.

questions.prompt: What does a missing child look like in the node?
questions.explanation: NULL means nothing is attached there.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
questions.explanation: These words describe how nodes relate.

questions.prompt: Root 5 has children 3 and 8. How many leaves are there in that tiny tree of three nodes?
questions.explanation: 3 and 8 have no children, so both are leaves.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to make a root with a left child.
steps: Free the child, then the root, later
questions.explanation: Link the child after creating both. Free children before their parent's pointer is lost.
